Stockholm+50: a healthy planet for the prosperity 
of all – our responsibility, our opportunity
Stockholm, 2 and 3 June 2022
Summary of stakeholder contributions to Stockholm+50
I.
Background
1.
Pursuant to General Assembly resolution 75/326, the international meeting “Stockholm+50: a 
healthy planet for the prosperity of all – our responsibility, our opportunity” was held in Stockholm on 
2 and 3 June 2022. It comprised an opening segment, four plenary meetings, three leadership 
dialogues and a closing segment. 
2.
The international meeting was the culmination of many months of preparatory work involving 
a wide variety of stakeholders. It was complemented by numerous side events (including special 
events and associated events) that aimed to capture the ideas and views of and pledges and proposals 
for action by Member States and stakeholders on a broad range of priority matters. 
3.
These preparatory activities and side events were an important part of the organization of the 
international meeting. In paragraph 13 of resolution 75/326, the General Assembly invited “all 
relevant stakeholders, including women, youth, older persons, persons with disabilities, indigenous 
peoples and local communities, to contribute to the discussions of the international meeting and their 
preparation and to build momentum for a healthy planet for the prosperity of all”. That was realized 
through a unique and inclusive open architecture of engagement that gave ownership to the global 
community to shape their views and make their voices heard in Stockholm. The bottom-up and co-
-creative facilitation allowed for truly inclusive multi-stakeholder engagement and a real sense of 
partnership. 
4.
The present document sets out a summary of the various engagements and consultations by 
different stakeholder groups with support from partners and United Nations agencies delivered at the 
international meeting. 
II.
Regional and national consultations
A.
Regional multi-stakeholder consultations
5.
In the lead-up to the Stockholm+50 international meeting, a series of regional 
multi-stakeholder consultations were organized in Africa; Asia and the Pacific; Europe; 
North America, Latin America and the Caribbean; and Western Asia. The consultations were 
organized by the Global Opportunities for Sustainable Development Goals (GO4SDGs) initiative and 
co-designed in close cooperation with the Major Groups and Stakeholders civil society grouping of the 
United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP). 
6.
The objectives of the regional consultations were to give voice to and facilitate the engagement 
of stakeholders and to ensure a bottom-up approach in mapping ongoing initiatives and key actions 
needed to safeguard our planet and promote action required in the sectors that are most critical for

sustainable development. Over 2,000 people participated in the consultations, providing input for both 
regional and global recommendations.
(a)
Synthesis report of the regional consultations: 
www.greengrowthknowledge.org/sites/default/files/2022-05/stockholm_50_synthesis.pdf. 
(b)
Detailed reports of the five regional consultations: 
www.stockholm50.global/processes/regional-multi-stakeholder-consultations.
B.
National multi-stakeholder consultations
7.
The national consultations aimed to stimulate an inclusive, whole-of-society and whole-of-
government dialogue on the themes of Stockhom+50 and the leadership dialogues. The United Nations 
Development Programme (UNDP) provided technical support to Stockholm+50 national consultations 
in 56 countries, facilitated by its country offices. More than 250 Stockholm+50 national events were 
organized, supported by online dialogues on UNDP’s SparkBlue Platform 
(www.sparkblue.org/stockholm50). Over 50,000 people participated in the consultations, either online 
or in person.
8.
The details of the national consultations can be found at: www.stockholm50.global/news-and-
stories/outcomes-stockholm50-national-consultations. The global synthesis report of the findings and 
insights from the national consultations will be published by UNDP later in 2022. More information 
on the national consultations can be found at: www.stockholm50.global/processes/national-
consultations-0. 
9.
A survey was distributed via UNDP country offices and other United Nations and partner 
networks in multiple languages to offer an additional opportunity for opinions to be shared: 
www.stockholm50.global/state-planet-global-public-survey. 
III.
Stakeholder engagements
10.
Many stakeholder contributions are featured on the dedicated page of the Stockholm+50 
website: www.stockholm50.global/participate/stakeholder-engagement. The main outcomes for each 
of the work streams are set out below.
A.
“Towards Stockholm+50”: a major groups and stakeholders project 
11.
A major groups and stakeholders-led initiative was supported by UNEP through a project 
entitled “Towards Stockholm+50”, aimed at engaging a wide variety of non-State actors globally to 
raise awareness of the legacy of 50 years of implementing environmental policies. A series of 
webinars and a podcast were organized prior to the international meeting and a side event was held on 
the margins of the meeting.
12.
The project also supported the regional multi-stakeholder consultations, and in the spirit of 
joint organization and knowledge exchange, support and information was provided to major groups 
and stakeholders through the project prior to both the international meeting and its preparatory 
meeting:
(a)
Towards Stockholm+50 project: towardstockholm50.org/;
(b)
Related webinars: towardstockholm50.org/events/;
(c)
Support to Stockholm+50 regional multi-stakeholder consultations: 
towardstockholm50.org/regional-meetings/.
13.
A “People’s Environment Narrative” document is being produced that will summarize the 
online consultations and encapsulate reports from the Stockholm+50 preparatory meeting held in 
New York on 28 March 2022, the seven expert webinars held by the “Towards Stockholm+50” 
initiative and the regional multi-stakeholder consultations organized in Africa; Asia and the Pacific; 
Europe; North America, Latin America and the Caribbean; and Western Asia. The report will be 
available on the towardstockholm50.org website and at unep.org/civil-society-engagement.
B.
Academic and research community
14.
Stockholm+50: Unlocking a Better Future: An independent scientific report authored by 
Stockholm Environment Institute and the Council on Energy, Environment and Water: 
www.stockholm50.report/.

15.
Academic conference: “Sustainable planet, sustainable health – how science-based solutions 
can drive transformative change”, co-organized by Stockholm University, KTH Royal Institute of 
Technology and Stockholm Environment Institute on 1 June 2022: www.sei.org/events/conference-
sustainable-planet-sustainable-health/.
16.
Green Growth Knowledge Platform: a four-part webinar series inviting leading champions 
from Governments, non-governmental organizations, international organizations, civil society and 
industry to exchange insights on themes relevant to Stockholm+50: 
www.greengrowthknowledge.org/news/ggkpwebinar-series-road-stockholm50.
(a)
Recordings are available on the Platform’s Stockholm+50 playlist; 
(b)
The webinars were complemented by the Stockholm+50 online community, offering 
space for exchange and collaboration amongst global stakeholders from all countries, regions, sectors 
and special interest groups; 
(c)
The Platform also published a series of Stockholm+50-focused “Insights” blogs from 
environmental and sustainability experts, practitioners and enthusiasts, to inform discussion and build 
momentum towards the international meeting. 
17.
A “Letter to fellow citizens of Earth”, modelled on the “Menton Message”, which was signed 
by a group of 2,200 environmental scientists from 23 countries on the eve of the United Nations 
Conference on the Human Environment, held in Stockholm from 5 to 16 June 1972, was tabled by a 
group of scientists following an expert group meeting held in Stockholm on 1 June 2022 and also 
published in the journal Nature: science4stockholm50.world/ and www.nature.com/articles/d41586-
022-01511-7.
C.
Business and industry
18.
Business and industry engagement was led by the World Business Council for Sustainable 
Development and Stockholm Environment Institute, under the overarching theme of sustainable value 
chains. 
(a)
Stockholm Action Agenda: Transforming Global Value Chains (based on the outcome 
of business round tables): www.wbcsd.org/Overview/Policy-Advocacy-and-Member-Mobilization-
PAMM/Resources/The-Stockholm-Action-Agenda-Transforming-Global-Value-Chains; 
(b)
A wide-ranging global survey (now closed) was conducted on sustainable value chains. 
D.
Indigenous peoples and local communities 
19.
In preparation for the international meeting, a series of in-person and virtual consultations 
were held on various matters, including the rights of indigenous peoples, local communities and 
environmental defenders; indigenous women; indigenous youth; and food systems. 
20.

E.
Interfaith
21.
Faith-based organizations established an interfaith working group to support faith 
communities' understanding of, and engagement in, issues related to Stockholm+50. The aim of the 
group was to facilitate networking and in-person collaboration, and to inspire and build partnerships 
between faith groups and civil society, indigenous groups and all other stakeholders. Stockholm+50 
Interfaith Statement: “Faith values and reach – contribution to environmental policy”: 
wedocs.unep.org/bitstream/handle/20.500.11822/40048/Stockholm%2b50%20Interfaith%20Statement
%2025%20May%202022.pdf?sequence=1&isAllowed=y. 
22.
Faith for Earth dialogue session at Stockholm+50, Nairobi and online, 4 March 2022.
23.
More details about faith-led events at Stockholm+50 are available on a dedicated page of the 
UNEP website: www.unep.org/faith-based-engagement-stockholm50. 
F.
Subnational and local authorities
24.
Cities and local authorities also participated in the national and regional consultations. They 
also organized the Cities Stockholm+50 High-level Forum, held in Stockholm on 1 and 2 June 2022.

G.
Empowerment of women and gender equality
26.
The Stockholm+50 national consultations, convened by UNDP, included discussions on 
gender responsiveness and social inclusivity. The Women’s Major Group (accredited to UNEP: 
www.unep.org/civil-society-engagement/major-groups-modalities/major-group-categories/women) 
was also engaged in the regional consultations and contributed to discussions on gender-responsive 
environmental management policies. The United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the 
Empowerment of Women (UN-Women) participated in the discussions at the informal working groups 
for the leadership dialogues and contributed to the integration of gender equality and women’s 
perspectives into the recommendations made by those groups. One of the Green Growth Knowledge 
Platform blogs also featured gender equality: www.greengrowthknowledge.org/blog/can-
stockholm50-be-turning-point-gender-equality. 
27.
At the international meeting, a number of side events on gender equality were held:
(a)
United Nations Special Rapporteur on the rights to freedom of peaceful assembly and 
of association: Resistance and resilience – enhancing civic space for women and girls in climate 
activism; 
(b)
Women’s Learning Partnership and others: Women on the frontlines of climate 
change: reports from the field and strategies for action: learningpartnership.org/events/stockholm-50-
women-frontlines-climate-change-reports-from-field-and-strategies-for-action;
(c)
International Development Law Organization, Swedish International Development 
Cooperation Agency, Government of Peru, Rights and Resources Initiative, UN-Women and 
Generation Equality Action Coalition on Feminist Action for Climate Justice: Feminist climate justice 
– empowering women and girls through the rule of law: www.idlo.int/news/events/stockholm50;
(d)
Green Growth Knowledge Platform Gender Expert Group: Achieving a Healthy Planet 
for all through a Gender-Just Recovery. www.greengrowthknowledge.org/event/stockholm50-side-
event-achieving-healthy-planet-all-through-gender-just-recovery. 
H.
Youth
28.
The Stockholm+50 Youth Task Force was established as a self-coordinated initiative and was 
instrumental in organizing many activities, including the Stockholm+50 Youth Assembly, and 
producing the Stockholm+50 Global Youth Policy Paper. More information on its work is available on 
the dedicated website of the Task Force at www.youthstockholm50.global/.

I.
United Nations entities and multilateral environmental agreements
29.
In November 2021, the Environment Management Group organized a two-part 
United Nations-wide virtual dialogue on the ways in which Stockholm+50 could empower the 
United Nations system to collectively move forward. The Dialogue highlighted the personal 
reflections of a diverse array of people who had worked with the United Nations system in many 
different capacities on lessons learned since 1972. It also explored their recommendations on the 
future implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development and produced two 
reports.

V.

disciplines and societies, creating a space to recast the human relationship with the environment and 
inform future policymaking.

VIII.
Associated events
37.
A broad range of associated events were independently organized and provided an opportunity 
for stakeholders to convene Stockholm+50-related events in association with the international 
meeting. The format and location of such events was flexible and they could be held in person, 
virtually or in a hybrid format, anywhere in the world, complementing the international meeting and 
promoting inclusiveness by bringing together and showcasing valuable ideas from diverse voices and 
contexts on a global stage.
Calendar of associated events:
www.stockholm50.global/events?Title=&type_of_event=Associated+Event.
